finish a tender report and, on the same afternoon, to sit on an interview
panel in another building. Doing one makes the other impossible.

A. Role conflict.
B. Punctuated equilibrium.
C. Storming.
D. Group cohesiveness.
E. Groupthink.

engineers' technical skills very highly, yet most client projects finish late
and over budget.

A. An ideal structure needing no change.

C. A shortage of technical certification
D. Budgets that were set too generously.

Question: Which advantage of the traditional structure does this reflect?
A. One person responsible for each project.
B. Easier budgeting and cost control.
C. Higher motivation and innovation.
D. Fast response to customer needs.
E. A single customer focal point.

Question: Which weakness of the traditional structure does this show?
A. Excessive project authority.
B. Too many bosses per employee.
C. Too few specialists to share.
D. Weak technical control.
E. No customer focal point.

E. Liaison department duties.

C. The team reflects at regular intervals to improve.
D. Requirements changes are welcome even late on.
E. Simplicity maximizes the amount of work not done.

developers on an XP team first write automated checks that the code

another.

C. Task switching.

choose the technical steps and tools, trusting their expertise rather than
dictating the approach.

A. Optimize the whole.
B. Defer decisions. C. Deliver fast.
D. Amplify learning.
E. Empower the team.

developers into unplanned meetings. The agile leader asks him to route
requests through her instead.

team inside the Scrum Team, with its own lead who reports to a senior
developer.
Question: Which response is consistent with Scrum?
A. Accept it, since testers need a separate lead to stay focused.
B. Accept it, since cross-functional teams need specialized sub-units.
C. Accept it, if the Scrum Master approves the reporting line.
D. Reject it, since a Scrum Team has no sub-teams or hierarchies.
E. Reject it, since testing should be done by the Product Owner.

heads to act jointly as the Product Owner for a new licensing system.
Question: What is the main problem with this arrangement from a
Scrum perspective?
A. The Product Owner must be a member of the Developers.
B. The Product Owner must be one person, not a committee.
C. Deputy heads lack the technical skills to size items.
D. A committee cannot attend the Daily Scrum every day.
E. The committee should include the Scrum Master as chair.
